newsitem.title: BELGIUM: PetroFina seen rising on profit jump.
newsitem.headline: PetroFina seen rising on profit jump.

text.p: Belgian oil and gas group PetroFina SA said on Tuesday higher oil prices and improved refining margins helped lift 1996 earnings by around 38 percent.
The shares are expected to rise on Wednesday, analysts said. The results were announced after the close of trading on the Brussels stock exchange.

Announcing provisional results, PetroFina said 1996 group net profit would be around 16.0 billion Belgian francs, up from 11.6 billion in 1995. Cash flow was estimated at 45 billion Belgian francs, or 1,935 francs a share, compared with 39 billion francs, or 1,691 francs a share.
"On first view these results look very good. Everyone will have to revise upwards their earnings expectations," Generale Bank analyst Sandra Vandersmissen told Reuters.
Vandersmissen noted PetroFina's cash flow was now back to the level it was at before 1992, when the company halved its dividend, provoking a long decline in its share prices.
"I think the share price will rise tomorrow," Vandersmissen said. PetroFina ended up 50 francs at 11,350 francs on the Brussels Stock Exchange.

PetroFina said the rise in results was mainly due to its upstream and downstream sectors. Operating profit in exploration and production rose to 23.8 billion francs from 13.2 billion francs. Earnings from refining and marketing were 4.3 billion francs, up from 0.1 billion francs in 1995.
But operating profit from the chemicals sector, which was PetroFina's main earner in 1995, slipped to 11.0 billion francs from 19.7 billion as margins came under pressure.
The company normally releases final results, as well as its dividend proposal, towards the end of March.
